# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Weekly Report (May 31 - June 6, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused heavily on hardening interoperability (interop) infrastructure and advancing devnet stability. Significant progress was made in validating interop proof paths, with a successful withdrawal proven on a forked devnet environment. However, development also uncovered critical synchronization and failsafe recovery challenges within the `op-supernode` and `op-reth` stack, leading to the proposal of new recovery runbooks and observability metrics. Routine maintenance continued via automated configuration updates to ensure registry consistency.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Interoperability & Devnet Progress
The team achieved a major milestone in the "Interop Proofs Devnet" by successfully proving a withdrawal, confirming the functional integrity of the withdrawal path in a forked environment ([#20489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20489)). Additionally, local devnet instances are now operational, with efforts shifting toward establishing a long-running devnet to support more rigorous testing ([#20691](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20691)).

### Infrastructure & Registry Maintenance
Routine automated code generation was performed to maintain the integrity of the registry. These updates modified `addresses.json` to ensure that chain configurations and contract addresses remain up-to-date across the ecosystem ([#1249](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1249), [#1250](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1250)).

### Protocol Synchronization & Compatibility
Discussions regarding `op-revm` support highlighted the team's commitment to staying in sync with the latest `revm` releases (v111), specifically regarding shared type definitions for the Amsterdam hardfork ([#21069](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21069)). This work is being coordinated alongside `reth` and `alloy-*` crate updates to ensure stack-wide compatibility.

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Interop Proofs:** Successfully closed the devnet proof validation issue after verifying the withdrawal path ([#20489](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/20489)).
*   **Security Audit:** Addressed feedback from the Lumi Security Audit regarding `doc.go` ([#21124](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21124)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Interop Recovery & Failsafes:** A critical issue was identified where the `op-reth` transaction pool fails to resume after an interop-filter failsafe is disabled. Current remediation requires a full restart of both `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder` ([#21149](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21149)). In response, a new runbook is being developed to handle chain recovery following invalid interop messages ([#21161](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21161)).
*   **Synchronization Stalls:** Investigation continues into `op-supernode` and `op-reth` synchronization failures. One issue involves the Consensus Layer (CL) stalling when bookkeeping references missing Execution Layer (EL) blocks ([#21076](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21076)). Another concerns `op-supernode` getting stuck if the EL is unreachable at startup, prompting a proposal to decouple engine-controller initialization ([#21136](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21136)).
*   **Backlog Processing:** Issues were noted regarding the inability of `cross-safe` to drain backlogs faster than real-time after a stall, particularly when the sequencing window expires ([#21117](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21117)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week saw active technical coordination between contributors like **joshklop**, **wodann**, **sebastianst**, and **ajsutton**. Collaboration was particularly high regarding the `op-reth` and `op-rbuilder` interaction, where cross-component debugging was necessary to identify why interop functionality remained "stuck" after failsafe events. The community is also focusing on improving system observability, as evidenced by the proposal for a new failsafe-state gauge metric ([#21151](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/21151)).
